55948.subject: Technical Drawing
55948.question_text: Construct a perpendicular bisector to a given line segment AB of length 60 mm using only a compass and a straightedge. Label all construction lines and points clearly.
55948.explanation:
1. Draw line segment AB = 60 mm.
2. With A as center and radius greater than half of AB, draw arcs above and below AB.
3. With B as center and the same radius, draw arcs intersecting the previous arcs at points C and D.
4. Draw a straight line through points C and D. This line is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
5. Label the intersection of the bisector with AB as point M, the midpoint of AB.
6. Ensure all construction arcs and lines are visible and labeled.

55949.subject: Technical Drawing
55949.question_text: Construct a regular hexagon with a side length of 30 mm using only a compass and a straightedge. Show all construction lines and label the vertices A, B, C, D, E, and F.
55949.explanation:
1. Draw a circle with radius 30 mm.
2. Mark a point A on the circumference.
3. Using the same radius, step off points B, C, D, E, and F around the circumference.
4. Join the points A, B, C, D, E, and F with straight lines to form the hexagon.
5. Label all vertices and ensure construction lines are visible.

55950.subject: Technical Drawing
55950.question_text: Construct a tangent to a given circle of radius 25 mm from an external point P located 50 mm from the center of the circle. Show all construction lines and label the point of tangency T.
55950.explanation:
1. Draw the given circle with center O and radius 25 mm.
2. Mark the external point P 50 mm from O.
3. Draw line OP.
4. Construct the perpendicular bisector of OP to find its midpoint M.
5. With M as center and radius OM, draw a semicircle intersecting the given circle at point T.
6. Draw line PT, which is the required tangent.
7. Label the point of tangency T and ensure all construction lines are visible.

55951.subject: Technical Drawing
55951.question_text: Draw the front, top, and right-side views of the given object in first-angle orthographic projection. The object is a rectangular block 50 mm × 30 mm × 20 mm with a semicircular slot of radius 10 mm cut into the top face along the 50 mm length. Show all hidden details using dashed lines.
55951.explanation:
1. Draw the front view showing the full height (20 mm) and length (50 mm) with the semicircular slot (radius 10 mm) at the top.
2. Draw the top view showing the length (50 mm) and width (30 mm) with the semicircular slot visible.
3. Draw the right-side view showing the height (20 mm) and width (30 mm) with the semicircular slot as a hidden detail (dashed line).
4. Ensure all views are aligned and dimensioned correctly.
5. Use appropriate line types: continuous for visible edges, dashed for hidden edges.

55952.subject: Technical Drawing
55952.question_text: Draw a full sectional front view of the given object, which is a hollow cylinder with an external diameter of 60 mm, internal diameter of 40 mm, and height of 50 mm. The section plane passes through the axis of the cylinder. Use appropriate hatching to indicate the cut surface.
55952.explanation:
1. Draw the front view of the cylinder as a rectangle 60 mm wide (external diameter) and 50 mm high.
2. Draw the internal diameter as a rectangle 40 mm wide and 50 mm high inside the external rectangle.
3. Draw the section plane line through the axis of the cylinder.
4. Hatch the area between the external and internal diameters to indicate the cut surface.
5. Ensure the hatching is at a 45° angle and evenly spaced.

55953.subject: Technical Drawing
55953.question_text: Draw an isometric view of a rectangular block measuring 40 mm × 30 mm × 20 mm. The block has a circular hole of diameter 15 mm drilled through the center of the top face. Show all hidden details using dashed lines.
55953.explanation:
1. Draw the isometric axes at 30° to the horizontal.
2. Construct the isometric box with dimensions 40 mm (length), 30 mm (width), and 20 mm (height).
3. On the top face, draw an ellipse to represent the circular hole (diameter 15 mm) using the isometric scale.
4. Show the hidden edges of the hole using dashed lines.
5. Ensure all lines are drawn to scale and the isometric projection is accurate.

55954.subject: Technical Drawing
55954.question_text: Develop the lateral surface of a right circular cone with a base diameter of 50 mm and a slant height of 60 mm. Show all construction lines and label the development clearly.
55954.explanation:
1. Calculate the circumference of the base: $C = \pi imes d = \pi imes 50$ mm.
2. Draw a sector of a circle with radius equal to the slant height (60 mm) and arc length equal to the circumference of the base.
3. The angle of the sector is calculated as $ heta = rac{C}{2 imes ext{slant height}} imes 360°$.
4. Draw the sector and label the arc and radii.
5. Ensure all construction lines are visible and the development is accurate.

55955.subject: Technical Drawing
55955.question_text: Draw the line of intersection between a vertical cylinder of diameter 40 mm and a horizontal cylinder of diameter 30 mm, where the axes of the two cylinders intersect at right angles. Show the front and top views of the intersection.
55955.explanation:
1. Draw the front view of the vertical cylinder (40 mm diameter) and the horizontal cylinder (30 mm diameter) intersecting at right angles.
2. In the top view, project the points of intersection from the front view.
3. Draw the line of intersection in both views, ensuring it is smooth and accurate.
4. Use appropriate line types: continuous for visible edges, dashed for hidden edges.
5. Label all key points and ensure the views are aligned.

55956.subject: Technical Drawing
55956.question_text: Dimension the following orthographic views of a simple bracket: front view (height 50 mm, width 40 mm) and side view (depth 20 mm). The bracket has a 10 mm diameter hole located 15 mm from the top and 20 mm from the left edge in the front view. Apply standard dimensioning conventions.
55956.explanation:
1. In the front view, dimension the overall height (50 mm) and width (40 mm).
2. Dimension the hole: diameter (10 mm), vertical position (15 mm from top), and horizontal position (20 mm from left edge).
3. In the side view, dimension the depth (20 mm).
4. Use extension lines, dimension lines, and arrowheads correctly.
5. Ensure dimensions are placed outside the views where possible and aligned neatly.

55957.subject: Technical Drawing
55957.question_text: Using a CAD software, draw a 2D orthographic projection of the given object (a rectangular plate 80 mm × 50 mm with two 12 mm diameter holes, each located 20 mm from the nearest edges). Include the front and top views, and apply appropriate layers for visible and hidden lines. Export the drawing as a DXF file and label it correctly.
55957.explanation:
1. Set up the CAD drawing with appropriate units (millimeters).
2. Draw the front view: rectangle 80 mm × 50 mm with two circles (diameter 12 mm) positioned 20 mm from the edges.
3. Draw the top view: rectangle 80 mm × 50 mm with the holes represented as hidden lines (dashed).
4. Use separate layers for visible lines (continuous) and hidden lines (dashed).
5. Ensure all dimensions and labels are clear and the drawing is exported as a DXF file.
